extracted.intended_audience: scientists, students, and authors/readers of scientific/technical handbooks (readers of Nature)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for preparing and judging scientific or technical handbooks and monographs—what such books should include, how they should be organized, and stylistic/content pitfalls to avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and conciseness of exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: The information should be conveyed in a manner that is both clear and concise—'admirably clear and full, yet concise'—so readers can readily understand the investigations and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present full statements of investigations and their results without unnecessary verbosity; aim for prose that is simultaneously detailed and succinct so the material is accessible and useful to students and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, classified bibliography linked to original sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an extensive classified bibliography that directs the reader to the original and full sources of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide thorough reference lists so students and researchers can consult primary literature; classify and organise bibliographic entries for ease of use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous illustrations, whether original or taken from the best monographs, add greatly to a work's usefulness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, relevant figures, plates or diagrams to elucidate structural and cytological points; illustrations should support the text and be chosen from reliable sources when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical and convenient organization/structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The book's internal arrangement should be convenient and coherent—organisation into chapters and sections is generally preferable to a highly irregular sequence of lectures of very unequal length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure material into appropriately sized chapters/sections, avoiding arbitrary fragmentary divisions (e.g., many very unequal 'lectures') that impede readability and navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship and familiarity with recent and classical research
rubrics_metrics.description: Author should show a remarkable familiarity with both the most recent and the classical researches relevant to the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and synthesize contemporary and foundational work; demonstrate awareness of ongoing debates and key historical studies to ground the exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate caution in generalization and theory extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not overextend theoretical conclusions beyond what the available data securely support—be cautious where 'the known is still too limited' to permit universal application of a criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State assumptions and limits of evidence clearly; highlight where conclusions are tentative and where further data are needed to substantiate general claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulating inquiry and including important discussions
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuable work should awaken inquiry in readers and introduce important discussions of wide interest that will stimulate further research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include sections that pose questions, compare competing views, and point to areas where further investigation is desirable; use illustrative discussions to provoke thoughtful follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize verbatim quotations; prefer summaries with references
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid excessive verbatim quotation from other works; long reproduced passages make the whole less coherent and are inappropriate for a handbook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the relevant content of other papers concisely and give clear references to the originals. If long passages are quoted, retain only essential excerpts and provide summaries of their results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherent synthesis of facts and theories (literary and scientific homogeneity)
rubrics_metrics.description: A handbook should 'weld' existing facts and theories into a consistent whole possessing both literary and scientific homogeneity, rather than being a patchwork of quoted texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate material through original narrative and analysis so chapters flow and the book presents a unified viewpoint; ensure consistent style and voice throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selectivity and editing of external material
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and edit material drawn from other sources—avoid reproducing long, uninteresting official correspondence or entire long descriptive articles when a summary will do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only the externally-sourced material that adds clear value; when reporting tests or systems described elsewhere, condense to essentials and cite the full reports for readers who need them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity of content to the format's function
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize the distinct functions of formats: books/handbooks are expected to synthesize and summarize existing facts/theories rather than to present primary new discoveries (which belong in journals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match scope and depth of content to the medium—handbooks should prioritize coherent summaries, didactic exposition, and practical organization over exhaustive reprints of primary-source material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concise summaries of long material
rubrics_metrics.description: When long works are discussed or quoted, provide a brief summary of the results—'we are told that the results may be summarised in a few words—the summary occupies sixteen lines.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a succinct distilled summary of key findings when referring to lengthy external texts; if a long quotation is retained, follow it with or replace it by a compact summary and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and focus of individual chapters
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure individual chapters are well-crafted and valuable; distinct, strong chapters (e.g., on key theories) can redeem otherwise weaker parts of a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Devote care to the development of central chapters—ensure they contain well-reasoned, self-contained discussions that address theory and application clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of illustrative examples across groups to clarify theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ examples (including comparative examples across taxa or systems) to illuminate theoretical points—e.g., using Volvox or Hydrodictyon to discuss heredity and reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose examples that concretely demonstrate abstract ideas; where helpful, draw parallels from different systems to make general principles clearer to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss functions and components in sufficient detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the functions of structures (e.g., cell components) and consider relevant physiological or cytological concepts (such as vacuoles, tonoplasts, granules) where they illuminate the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide focused discussions of key components and their functional significance; balance technical detail with accessibility so non-specialist readers can follow the implications.
